_meta.description: Per-zone planting calendars for GNA's five Zambian agroecological zones. Day ranges are days_since_planting. Each zone has its own planting_window because rainfall onset and soil temperature differ. Topics + templates are reused across zones except where the agronomic guidance varies (e.g. Zone IIa needs more aggressive weed management due to higher pest pressure; Zone III gets later top-dressing because rainfall extends longer).

_zone_meta.name: Eastern Plateau
_zone_meta.notes: Smallest cohort (134 farmers) but reasonable yields. Plant early to capture full rains.

day_0_7.template: Confirm inoculant applied at planting. Mention the +545 kg/ha lift this gives Zone I farmers (highest of any zone). Ask about seed quantity used.

day_8_14.template: Ask about row spacing. Ideal is 45-50cm for soy bean. Encourage if on track.

day_15_30.template: First weeding reminder. Weeds in first 30 days steal nutrients. Ask if they have weeded.

day_31_45.template: Ask farmer to check for pests. Eastern Plateau sees pod borer + stink bug most often. Describe holes, discolouration.

day_46_60.template: Top-dressing fertilizer reminder if in loan package. Apply now while rains are still reliable.

day_61_75.template: Pods should be forming. Ask farmer to count pods on a sample plant. If <20 pods, may indicate pollination stress.

day_76_90.template: Maturity approaches. Pods turning yellow-brown, leaves dropping = ready in 7-10 days. Discuss harvest plan.

day_91_120.template: Confirm harvest date. Remind: drying to 12% moisture before delivery. Confirm buyback collection logistics.

_zone_meta.name: Central Plateau
_zone_meta.notes: Largest cohort (15,952 farmers) and lowest median yield. 81% of all high-risk farmers concentrate here. Highest priority zone for field-agent contact.

day_0_7.template: Confirm inoculant applied. In Zone IIa, inoculant adds about +191 kg/ha after zone control. Combined with training, much higher.

day_8_14.template: Row spacing check. 45-50cm for soy bean. Zone IIa farmers benefit most from precise spacing because every kg counts.

day_15_30.template: Weeding window. Zone IIa has higher weed pressure than other zones. Hoe between rows. Untreated weeds = direct yield loss.

day_25_35.template: Zone IIa drought risk window. Ask if rainfall has been adequate. If leaves are curling or soil is dry, advise mulching to retain moisture.

day_31_45.template: Pest scouting. Zone IIa sees soybean aphid + pod borer. Check leaves for holes. >5 insects/plant = apply insecticide.

day_46_60.template: Top-dressing reminder. In Zone IIa, fertilizer x training together is the strongest yield lever. Apply now.

day_61_75.template: Pod-formation check. With Zone IIa's variable rains, water stress at pod fill is the #1 cause of low yield. Mulch retains moisture.

day_76_90.template: Maturity nearing. Plan harvest. In Zone IIa, late-season heat can shatter pods, do not delay once pods are brown.

day_91_120.template: Confirm harvest. Drying to 12%. Buyback collection logistics. If farmer cannot fully repay in kind, flag immediately for soft renegotiation.

_zone_meta.name: Southern Plateau
_zone_meta.notes: Small cohort (442 farmers). Lower rainfall but higher per-farmer yield than IIa.

day_0_7.template: Confirm inoculant applied. Critical in IIb where soil nitrogen is often limiting.

day_8_14.template: Row spacing 45-50cm. Slightly wider OK in IIb to conserve soil moisture.

day_15_30.template: Weed early. In IIb's drier conditions, weeds compete heavily for moisture.

day_31_45.template: Mulch around plants if rainfall has been below average. IIb often experiences mid-season dry spells.

day_46_60.template: Top-dressing if in package. Apply just before expected rain to avoid scorch.

day_61_75.template: Pod fill stage. Water stress now causes pod abortion. If dry, irrigate if possible.

day_76_90.template: Maturity check. Plan harvest schedule. Drying may be faster in IIb.

day_91_120.template: Confirm buyback. Drying to 12%. Logistics confirmation.

_zone_meta.name: Northern Plateau
_zone_meta.notes: Highest median yield (848 kg/ha) but only 6,069 farmers. Lwangeni variety dominates and explains much of the lift.

day_0_7.template: Confirm seed variety. Lwangeni gives Zone III farmers the highest yields (1,200 kg/ha median). If using anything else, ask why.

day_8_14.template: Row spacing 45-50cm. Zone III's longer rains support tighter spacing.

day_15_30.template: Weeding window. Zone III's high rainfall encourages rapid weed growth, weed twice in first 45 days.

day_31_45.template: Zone III high humidity = soybean rust risk. If fungicide is in your loan package, apply at first sign of yellow spots on lower leaves.

day_46_60.template: Top-dressing window. Zone III rains allow late application without scorch.

day_61_75.template: Pod-fill window. Zone III conditions usually favor heavy pod set. Check pod count on sample plants.

day_76_90.template: Approaching maturity. Zone III moisture means slower drying, plan accordingly.

day_91_125.template: Confirm harvest date. Drying may take longer due to Zone III humidity. Logistics confirmation.

_zone_meta.name: Western Plain
_zone_meta.notes: Sandy soils retain less water. Few GNA farmers in this zone.

day_0_7.template: Confirm inoculant. On sandy IV soils, inoculant + organic matter is essential.

day_8_14.template: Row spacing 45cm. Tight spacing helps shade soil and conserve moisture.

day_15_30.template: Mulch is critical on sandy IV soils. Cover bare soil between rows with crop residue.

day_31_45.template: Pest scouting. Aphids and thrips active. Check leaves daily.

day_46_60.template: Apply top-dressing after a rain event. Sandy soils leach nutrients quickly.

day_61_75.template: Pod-fill stage. Water stress = pod abortion on sandy soils.
